claims.claim: The selected pair explains a relevant biallelic BUB1B deficit.
claims.support: Gene-level MVA evidence and the permitted ranked pair motivate testing.
claims.challenge: Phase is unresolved; competition performance is not molecular validation; other causes remain possible.
claims.falsifier: Supported cis phase or a discordant, adequately measured endogenous functional phenotype.
claims.stop_rule: Do not attribute a trans-specific result to the subject while phase remains unknown.
claims.reopen_rule: Independent phase and allele-function evidence with an appropriate model.
claims.next_action: Keep subject phase unresolved; model-specific experiments can proceed without pretending engineered phase resolves the subject.
claims.v21_action: Keep subject phase unresolved; model-specific experiments can proceed without pretending engineered phase resolves the subject.

claims.claim: The stop allele is a null and the missense allele impairs endogenous function.
claims.support: Consequence and sequence evidence support a loss-of-function hypothesis.
claims.challenge: Transcript decay, residual protein and scaffold/checkpoint effects are unmeasured; cDNA overexpression bypasses endogenous RNA regulation.
claims.falsifier: Reproducible retained endogenous function, or a different mechanism, with valid positive controls.
claims.stop_rule: Suspend the specific null/folding mechanism if endogenous evidence disagrees; do not deny all disease mechanisms.
claims.reopen_rule: RNA, abundance, localization and checkpoint/attachment evidence resolve the mechanism.
claims.next_action: Add expression-matched correction and timing; failed assay controls mean invalid measurement, not a benign allele.
claims.v21_action: Add expression-matched correction and timing; failed assay controls mean invalid measurement, not a benign allele.

claims.claim: A negative protein language-model score establishes impaired function.
claims.support: All 12 newer model/window candidate scores are negative.
claims.challenge: Retained controls have negative scores in 11/24 comparisons; impaired controls have positive scores in 2/48.
claims.falsifier: Already observed counterexamples invalidate a universal sign cutoff.
claims.stop_rule: Reject sign-based pathogenicity or rescue selection.
claims.reopen_rule: An independently validated, context-specific calibration could support a bounded predictive claim.
claims.next_action: Do not use score sign as a functional label; preserve all favorable and unfavorable controls.
claims.v21_action: Do not use score sign as a functional label; preserve all favorable and unfavorable controls.

claims.claim: Confident, similar mutant structures establish normal function or a repairable folding defect.
claims.support: Several models consistently predict a confident fold.
claims.challenge: Impaired controls also fold confidently; domain-only structures omit full-length interactions, abundance and cell state.
claims.falsifier: Confident predictions for experimentally impaired controls already defeat the shortcut.
claims.stop_rule: Do not qualify a folding-rescue drug or binder from confidence/RMSD alone.
claims.reopen_rule: A measured repairable defect and validated intervention-specific functional assay.
claims.next_action: Further structure seeds cannot identify drug rescue; require a measured modifiable defect before binder work.
claims.v21_action: Further structure seeds cannot identify drug rescue; require a measured modifiable defect before binder work.

claims.claim: Atlas and Evo benchmarks supply independent BUB1B functional validation.
claims.support: Public benchmark and numerical checks succeeded.
claims.challenge: Reused evolutionary/annotation information and BRCA1 controls are not BUB1B transfer validation; window means change scale.
claims.falsifier: Failure on independent, biologically relevant BUB1B controls would defeat the transfer claim.
claims.stop_rule: No clinical classification, NMD, splicing, phase or drug inference from benchmark success.
claims.reopen_rule: Independent domain-relevant functional calibration with pretraining overlap assessed.
claims.next_action: Count evidence by independent biological experiment; benchmarks, reused annotations and model families are not replications.
claims.v21_action: Count evidence by independent biological experiment; benchmarks, reused annotations and model families are not replications.

claims.claim: Passing the small primary control gate establishes robust general predictive accuracy.
claims.support: The prespecified primary ordering passes 12/12 newer comparisons.
claims.challenge: Post-hoc inclusion of secondary controls fails complete separation in 8/12; one study and repeated residue 882 dominate retained-function coverage.
claims.falsifier: Control-set sensitivity is already observed; it does not invalidate the original narrow pass.
claims.stop_rule: Withdraw broad validation wording; retain primary success and sensitivity failures together.
claims.reopen_rule: An independent, representative functional panel and prospectively fixed evaluation.
claims.next_action: Predeclare an external blinded control set; do not optimize the threshold on the candidate or remove failed controls.
claims.v21_action: Predeclare an external blinded control set; do not optimize the threshold on the candidate or remove failed controls.

claims.claim: Branch A: excess mTOR signaling contributes to a modifiable functional deficit.
claims.support: Different-allele mouse muscle phosphoproteins motivate measuring the pathway.
claims.challenge: No selected-pair excess or benefit is established; excess can be adaptive and the mouse study did not test rapalog rescue.
claims.falsifier: No reproducible excess with adequate assay range, or inhibition worsens useful function.
claims.stop_rule: Stop branch A when its eligibility fails; unresolved measurements remain a hold, not disproof.
claims.reopen_rule: Reproducible functional deficit, excess and a locked benefit/harm perturbation.
claims.next_action: Require adequate dynamic range and a relevant deficit. Adaptive signaling remains an alternative; pathway suppression alone cannot pass.
claims.v21_action: Require adequate dynamic range and a relevant deficit. Adaptive signaling remains an alternative; pathway suppression alone cannot pass.

claims.claim: Branch B: correcting a flux/regenerative deficit could improve useful function without excess baseline mTOR.
claims.support: Hypercapnia experiments report rapamycin-associated functional benefit.
claims.challenge: Different disease and compound; supplement reports inconsistent ex vivo concentration units; no relevant deficit exists here yet.
claims.falsifier: No qualified flux/function deficit or no meaningful benefit under a valid, adequately informative test.
claims.stop_rule: Do not rescue failed A by switching to B; do not import an unresolved study concentration.
claims.reopen_rule: Independently qualify B and resolve source/exposure questions before an exposure-linked claim.
claims.next_action: Separate impaired clearance from insufficient induction; increasing initiation could worsen a downstream block. Qualify with orthogonal turnover and function.
claims.v21_action: Separate impaired clearance from insufficient induction; increasing initiation could worsen a downstream block. Qualify with orthogonal turnover and function.

claims.claim: Drug target engagement means the intended mechanism causes benefit.
claims.support: Pathway measurements can establish a bounded pharmacodynamic response.
claims.challenge: pS6 alone misses substrate-specific and feedback responses; genetic perturbations can differ in timing and extent.
claims.falsifier: Engagement without function, or discordance with an interpretable orthogonal perturbation.
claims.stop_rule: Reject biomarker-only rescue; restrict mechanism attribution when orthogonal results disagree.
claims.reopen_rule: Replicated functional effect with graded, time-matched mechanistic controls.
claims.next_action: Allow separately locked A or B; neither target engagement nor a second rapalog proves mediation. Avoid making A mandatory for valid B.
claims.v21_action: Allow separately locked A or B; neither target engagement nor a second rapalog proves mediation. Avoid making A mandatory for valid B.

claims.claim: Fewer abnormal surviving divisions demonstrate constitutional rescue.
claims.support: Accurate segregation is a relevant endpoint.
claims.challenge: Death, arrest, slippage, delayed daughter loss or tracking loss can improve a survivor fraction.
claims.falsifier: No gain in useful output per enrolled culture, or plausible missing-outcome bounds erase the claimed gain.
claims.stop_rule: Reject survivor-only rescue; distinguish absent benefit, harm and imprecision.
claims.reopen_rule: Prespecified gain with all fates retained and injury bounds met.
claims.next_action: Fix enrollment and follow-up; retain cell loss and bounds. Technical wells can be randomized units but are not additional donors/clones.
claims.v21_action: Fix enrollment and follow-up; retain cell loss and bounds. Technical wells can be randomized units but are not additional donors/clones.

claims.claim: A lower tumour IC50 than in deficient-normal cells establishes selectivity.
claims.support: Tumour response deserves a separate efficacy test.
claims.challenge: Different baseline division rates distort endpoint IC50; ATP signal is a proxy and normal cells may be slow or postmitotic.
claims.falsifier: Apparent selectivity disappears in direct counts/fates or growth-rate-aware analysis, or normal function worsens.
claims.stop_rule: No selectivity claim from endpoint ratios alone or undefined growth-rate normalization.
claims.reopen_rule: Matched exposure/time and justified functional normal-tissue bounds with a valid oncology comparator.
claims.next_action: Separate tumour and deficient-normal function at matched exposure; do not infer tumour subtype from the germline pair.
claims.v21_action: Separate tumour and deficient-normal function at matched exposure; do not infer tumour subtype from the germline pair.

claims.claim: A fluorescent or LC3 change establishes beneficial autophagic flux.
claims.support: Dynamic reporters and degradation measurements can interrogate flux.
claims.challenge: Reporter expression, acidity, lysosome abundance and compound optical interference can mimic flux changes.
claims.falsifier: The signal tracks pH/reporter abundance without corroborating cargo turnover or function.
claims.stop_rule: No flux or rescue inference from a single reporter or inhibitor-associated protein accumulation.
claims.reopen_rule: Orthogonal turnover and pH-aware assay qualification plus meaningful function.
claims.next_action: HCQ is not a selective flux control; check chromatin timing and orthogonal cargo turnover with interference controls.
claims.v21_action: HCQ is not a selective flux control; check chromatin timing and orthogonal cargo turnover with interference controls.

claims.claim: A successful culture concentration has an achievable, tolerable human tissue counterpart.
claims.support: Compound-specific PK and official-label observations inform feasibility.
claims.challenge: Whole blood, total plasma and nominal culture differ; free tissue time profiles and a normal-tissue window are unknown.
claims.falsifier: Benefit occurs only outside a justified exposure bound or at unacceptable injury.
claims.stop_rule: Hold translation with missing exposure; stop the tested exposure-linked claim if the bound fails.
claims.reopen_rule: Measured or defensibly bounded relevant free exposures with matched analyte, matrix and schedule.
claims.next_action: Keep every clinical margin null; resolve identity, analyte, matrix, free fraction and full time course before transfer.

claims.claim: A normal-tissue assay or an approved pediatric indication establishes safety for this context.
claims.support: Specified pediatric TSC indications and growth follow-up are favorable context-specific evidence.
claims.challenge: Kidney, immune, marrow, wound, muscle and developmental risks differ; no MVA margin is established.
claims.falsifier: Function or recovery exceeds prespecified injury limits in a relevant deficient-normal model.
claims.stop_rule: No advancement when safety bounds are failed or unresolved; nonsignificance is not noninferiority.
claims.reopen_rule: Adequately precise injury bounds and relevant context/exposure review.
claims.next_action: Use interval-based injury bounds, not nonsignificant p-values. Keep supportive growth evidence and official-label harms together.
claims.v21_action: Use interval-based injury bounds, not nonsignificant p-values. Keep supportive growth evidence and official-label harms together.

claims.claim: Improved short-term survival or proliferation implies durable developmental benefit.
claims.support: Useful cell output can be a valid bounded endpoint.
claims.challenge: Expansion may select damaged clones; mature tissues and developmental timing differ; neither risk nor benefit has been measured here.
claims.falsifier: Persistent chromosomal injury, harmful rebound, loss of mature function or selective expansion of unstable cells.
claims.stop_rule: Do not expand a short-term assay result into whole-development rescue or tumour safety.
claims.reopen_rule: Lineage-relevant recovery and longitudinal fidelity evidence in the intended scope.
claims.next_action: Track late clonal composition and recovery; protect against selection of rapidly expanding unstable cells.
claims.v21_action: Track late clonal composition and recovery; protect against selection of rapidly expanding unstable cells.

claims.claim: A positive exploratory result with many cells establishes reproducible benefit and safety.
claims.support: Blocked randomization, blinding and clustered analysis can support inference.
claims.challenge: Cells are nested; clones share a donor; small clusters, endpoint switching and imprecise safety tests can inflate certainty.
claims.falsifier: Effects disappear under clone/day sensitivity or do not exceed a meaningful benefit bound in independent confirmation.
claims.stop_rule: Hold underpowered/ambiguous results; reject the tested meaningful-effect claim only with adequate precision; retain safety stops.
claims.reopen_rule: Locked estimands, margins, replication units, multiplicity and independently collected confirmation.
claims.next_action: Lock benefit and injury estimands/margins before independent confirmation; distinguish invalid, inconclusive, futility and injury decisions.

claims.claim: The 0/14 filter result biologically falsifies BUB1B deficiency.
claims.challenge: Unknown sensitivity and arbitrary reagent minimum can reject genuine signal.
claims.falsifier: The same filter rejects independent known-positive on-target signatures.
claims.stop_rule: Reject biological interpretation of failed qualification.
claims.reopen_rule: External controls establish a useful error rate and transfer domain.
claims.v21_action: Calibrate on held-out controls before further ranking; retain HT29.

claims.claim: Whole-reagent null resampling gives calibrated causal significance.
claims.challenge: Seeds, potency, off-target and cell-state composition are unmatched.
claims.falsifier: Matched null or orthogonal genetics reverses the result.
claims.stop_rule: Do not label adjusted empirical tails as validated causal probabilities.
claims.reopen_rule: Prospectively matched controls and independent functional evidence.
claims.v21_action: Specify matched null and leave-seed/family-out validation when metadata allow; otherwise mark infeasible.
claims.support: Whole-reagent resampling retains each reagent vector and cell context, an improvement over treating genes as independent; 560,000 retained draws were audited.
claims.next_action: Specify matched null and leave-seed/family-out validation when metadata allow; otherwise mark infeasible.

claims.claim: The HT29 post-hoc tail 0.042 confirms the disease signature.
claims.challenge: Five reagents miss the six-reagent gate; branch selection and multiple transformations add researcher flexibility.
claims.falsifier: Independent held-out perturbations fail to replicate direction and function.
claims.stop_rule: Retain as exploratory; no relaxed threshold retrospectively.
claims.reopen_rule: New independent, locked confirmation.
claims.v21_action: Retain 0.042 alongside the failed full gate; no confirmation from reusing the same profiles.
claims.support: HT29 shared-pattern removal yields a favorable adjusted tail 0.0419958 and split consistency about 0.321 with five reagents; the predeclared full filter still fails.
claims.next_action: Retain 0.042 alongside the failed full gate; no confirmation from reusing the same profiles.

claims.claim: Everolimus-labelled profiles form one interpretable dose-response curve.

claims.reopen_rule: Identity-resolved, replicated concentration-time data with engagement.
claims.v21_action: No low-dose efficacy/harm inference; verify material separately from metadata.

claims.claim: Drug-only reversal predicts rescue in deficient cells.
claims.challenge: Disease and drug profiles were measured in separate perturbations; reversal can oppose compensation.
claims.falsifier: Joint exposure in qualified deficient cells has no meaningful function gain or harms them.
claims.stop_rule: No rescue claim from correlation.
claims.reopen_rule: Independent joint intervention with function and bounded injury.
claims.v21_action: Use direct joint experiments; compare corrected controls without demanding genotype-exclusive benefit.
claims.support: Perturbational transcriptomes measure a shared set of 978 landmarks and can nominate opposed expression patterns for follow-up.
claims.next_action: Use direct joint experiments; compare corrected controls without demanding genotype-exclusive benefit.

claims.claim: NAD/SIRT2 evidence identifies an approved BUBR1-restoration drug.
claims.challenge: NMN, niacin and nicotinamide differ; genetic survival and drug abundance results are separate. Residual mutant function is unknown.
claims.falsifier: Abundance rises without useful function, checkpoint timing worsens, or exposure/safety fails.
claims.stop_rule: No automatic promotion of a vitamin or SIRT2 intervention.
claims.reopen_rule: Compound-specific NAD/target/function mediation with residual functional protein and bounded injury.
claims.v21_action: Include an alternative branch only after qualification; S69-S72 adjudicate both directions.
claims.support: S69 reports genetic SIRT2 effects and separate NMN-associated BUBR1 abundance; S71 reports favorable muscle findings in a small open-label niacin study.
claims.next_action: Include an alternative branch only after qualification; S69-S72 adjudicate both directions.

claims.stop_rule: Exclude HCQ as the sole mechanistic positive control; keep reserve only.
claims.reopen_rule: Relevant exposure, flux corroboration, checkpoint function and normal-tissue safety.
claims.v21_action: Add explicit chromatin-compaction/decompaction and delayed injury tests before reopening.
claims.support: The preserved Goutas experiments report BUBR1 accumulation after HCQ and motivate an autophagy hypothesis; S66 supplies an independent chromatin-mechanism challenge.
claims.next_action: Add explicit chromatin-compaction/decompaction and delayed injury tests before reopening.

claims.reopen_rule: Direct, replicated intended-context evidence.
claims.v21_action: Measure schedule and recovery; never adopt intermittent dosing from unrelated organisms.
